bug_description.normalized: Poppler incorrectly reuses the dictionary backing a standalone widget annotation. `Page::loadStandaloneFields()` builds a synthetic standalone form field with `Object(annot->getDict())`, which wraps the annotation's borrowed `Dict *` in a new owning `Object` without incrementing the dictionary refcount. For a widget dictionary loaded from a compressed object stream, page teardown frees that shared dictionary through the standalone field before `XRef` destroys the cached `ObjectStream` entry. The later cached-object cleanup decrements the refcount field of the already-freed `Dict`, producing the observed heap-use-after-free write in `Object::free()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled compressed object-stream member is materialized as `objs[i]`, the cached owning `Object` later reused by `ObjectStream::~ObjectStream()` at the sink.

source.description: Parser starts materializing a dictionary for the attacker-controlled compressed object-stream member that will become the page's standalone widget annotation object.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled PDF bytes from `/mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_21604/poc`, specifically a compressed object-stream entry later referenced from a page `/Annots` array.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The standalone-field path wraps `annot->getDict()` in `Object(...)`, creating another owning `Object` for the same dictionary without calling `copy()` or otherwise incrementing the dict refcount. The shared dictionary is now owned by more `Object` instances than its refcount records. The fix replaces this with `annot->getAnnotObj().copy()`, which increments the refcount correctly.

sink.description: During `ObjectStream::~ObjectStream()` cleanup, the stale cached `Object` from the compressed object stream executes `dict->decRef()` on a dictionary that was already freed during page teardown, causing the ASan heap-use-after-free write to the freed refcount field.

fine_trace.note: After the attacker-controlled object-stream entry is recognized as a dictionary (`<<`), the parser allocates a fresh `Dict` object. Subsequent `dictSet` calls in the same parse fill this dictionary from the PoC's widget-annotation entries.

The fully parsed dictionary object is stored in `ObjectStream::objs[i]`, giving the compressed-object cache its persistent owning reference to the widget dictionary. This cached owner survives until `XRef` destruction.

When the page annotation array later fetches this compressed object, `copy()` increments the dictionary refcount and returns a second owning `Object`. `Annots::createAnnot()` moves that copy into `Annot::annotObj`, so the page annotation and the object-stream cache legitimately share the same dictionary.

The annotation has already passed the preceding `Widget` and `hasRef` checks, and `form->findWidgetByRef(r)` returns null. This sends the PoC down the standalone-field path instead of reusing an existing AcroForm widget.

Root cause. `annot->getDict()` returns the borrowed `Dict *` inside `Annot::annotObj`. Wrapping it in `Object(...)` uses the raw-pointer constructor, which does not increment the dictionary refcount, unlike `copy()`. The new standalone `FormField` therefore adds another owner for the same dictionary while leaving the shared refcount one too low.

The synthesized field passes the preceding retention gate (`field && field->getType() == formButton && field->getNumWidgets() == 1`), so Page keeps this undercounted standalone field alive until page teardown instead of deleting it immediately.

During page teardown, `delete annots;` at line 323 removes the normal annotation owner first. Then destroying the retained standalone field releases its undercounted dictionary owner; because step 5 missed one refcount increment, the `FormField` deletion chain reaches zero here and frees the shared dictionary even though `ObjectStream::objs[i]` still retains a cached owner.

Later `PDFDoc::~PDFDoc` deletes `xref`; `ObjectStream::~ObjectStream()` then destroys the cached `objs` array. The stale cached `Object` from step 2 calls `dict->decRef()` on the dictionary already freed in step 7, and ASAN reports a heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 4 in the dictionary refcount word.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC's compressed object stream is parsed successfully, and the widget annotation dictionary is cached in `objs[i]`.

standalone_button_retained.description: The widget is absent from the catalog form tree and parses as a single-widget button field, so Page retains it in `standaloneFields` for later teardown.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The fix removes the raw `Dict *` accessor used by this path and changes standalone-field creation from `Object(annot->getDict())` to `annot->getAnnotObj().copy()`. That preserves the extra owner but also increments the dictionary refcount, so page teardown no longer frees the dictionary before the cached `ObjectStream` owner is destroyed.

key_changes.change: Replaces `getDict()` with `getAnnotObj()` so callers can request a proper `Object::copy()` instead of borrowing a raw `Dict *`.
Changes `Form::createFieldFromDict(Object(annot->getDict()), ...)` to `Form::createFieldFromDict(annot->getAnnotObj().copy(), ...)`, restoring the missing refcount increment.

format.name: PDF with compressed standalone widget button annotation
format.contract: A PDF that loads far enough to parse a page annotation dictionary from a compressed object stream, where that annotation is `/Subtype /Widget`, has an object reference, is absent from the catalog AcroForm field tree, and parses as a single-widget button field so `Page::loadStandaloneFields()` retains it in `standaloneFields` before teardown.
